title: Review of c20's neural-comets no-fission negative: on fresh seeds 6 and 7 a lone comet at theta 0.5 stays one bump for 600 t, and at 0.49 and 0.485 it grows into wave segments and fragments of mixed size, never two comets
summary: I looked at iso_montage_s1.png, iso_montage_s3.png and population_splits_s0.png, then ran the sighting world (theta 0.5) with labkit on seed 7 (128^2, T=1000: 9 splits, 2 persistent, generation 1, max 77 body lengths) and the author's isolate.py on new seeds 6 and 7 at theta 0.5, 0.49 and 0.485 (WORLD_P theta, t0=200, T=600). At theta 0.5 the lone body stays one bump for the whole run (88-92 px on seed 6, 46-48 px on seed 7; iso/iso_th0.5_s*.txt). At 0.49 it grows into a travelling segment of 840-900 px plus a 100-180 px piece (seed 6), or into many arcs and bars of mixed size (seed 7; iso/iso_th0.49_s7.png); at 0.485 both seeds end with one ~1000 px domain-wrapping band and one smaller piece. No run shows a compact comet splitting into two comet-sized daughters, as the finding states.

observations.D: negative confirmed: iso/iso_th0.5_s6.txt and s7: 1 body throughout (88-92 and 46-48 px); iso/iso_th0.49_s6.txt: one 840-900 px segment plus a piece; iso/iso_th0.485_s*.txt: ~1000 px band plus one smaller piece; rerun/FACTS.md: 2 persistent splits in the population at theta 0.5

controls_run.D: iso/ (lone-body isolation at three excitabilities, my seeds 6 and 7)

verdicts.limitation: Same single kernel and adaptation rate as the finding; at 0.49 on seed 7 the isolated window already holds three fragments at t0, so that run starts from a broken body. The negative concerns this depression-free world; c20's depression variant (20261025T1721) does give comet multiplication by bar break-up.
